title: Brokers, KRaft and replication
summary: Leaders, followers, the ISR and the high watermark, and how acks and min.insync.replicas decide whether an acknowledged write survives a broker crash.

steps.title: A cluster: brokers, controllers and replicas
body: A Kafka cluster is a set of **brokers** (they store partitions and serve clients) plus a small **controller quorum**.
Since **Kafka 4.0 the cluster runs in KRaft mode only**: ZooKeeper is gone. Three (or five) controllers run Raft over
an internal metadata log (`__cluster_metadata`); the active controller decides which broker leads each partition and
pushes metadata changes to every broker.
```text
controllers (Raft quorum, process.roles=controller)
[ C1 active ]  [ C2 ]  [ C3 ]
| metadata: leaders, ISR, configs
v                 v                 v
broker 1           broker 2           broker 3
orders-0 LEADER    orders-0 follower  orders-0 follower     replication factor 3
orders-1 follower  orders-1 LEADER    orders-1 follower
orders-2 follower  orders-2 follower  orders-2 LEADER
producers write to the leader; followers FETCH from the leader, like consumers do
- Every partition has **replication factor** copies (3 in production). One is the **leader**; the others are
**followers** that keep fetching from it.
- The **ISR** (in-sync replicas) is the set of replicas that are caught up: a follower that has not caught up for
`replica.lag.time.max.ms` (30 s default) is removed from the ISR, and added back once it catches up.
- If the leader dies, the controller elects a new leader **from the ISR**. With `unclean.leader.election.enable=false`
(the default) an out-of-sync replica is never elected, so the partition goes offline rather than losing data.
- Leaders are spread over brokers so the load is spread too (`kafka-leader-election.sh --election-type preferred`
moves leadership back to the preferred replica after a restart).
Brokers are configured with `process.roles=broker`, controllers with `process.roles=controller`;
`process.roles=broker,controller` (combined mode) is for laptops and tests.

steps.prompt: Match each term to what it means.
pairs: The replica that handles produce requests for the partition
Copies the leader's log by fetching from it
The replicas that have caught up within `replica.lag.time.max.ms`
The offset every ISR member has reached; consumers read only below it
The Raft leader that owns cluster metadata and elects partition leaders
explain: Two offsets matter per partition: the **log-end offset** (where the leader will write next) and the **high
watermark** (what the whole ISR has). Records between the two exist on the leader but are not yet *committed*,
so consumers do not see them.

steps.title: The high watermark, acks and min.insync.replicas
body: The **high watermark** (HW) is the lowest log-end offset across the ISR. A record below the HW is on every in-sync
replica, so it survives the loss of the leader. Step through the program below to see the HW move when a slow
follower drops out of the ISR.
The producer's **`acks`** decides when the leader answers:
| `acks` | the leader answers when | an acknowledged write can be lost when |
| `0` | never (fire and forget) | anything goes wrong |
| `1` | it wrote to its own log | the leader dies before followers fetched it |
| `all` (`-1`) | every ISR member has it | only if the ISR had shrunk to one and that disk dies |
**`min.insync.replicas`** (topic or broker config) closes that last gap: with `acks=all`, the leader **refuses** the
write with `NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS` when the ISR is smaller than it. The production default is **RF 3 +
min.insync.replicas 2 + acks=all**: one broker can be down and writes still succeed, and every acknowledged write
is on at least two disks. `min.insync.replicas` has **no effect on acks=1**.
Defaults: the Java producer uses `acks=all` since Kafka 3.0; librdkafka (Confluent.Kafka) also defaults to `acks=all`.
> **See it:** in **Labs → Messaging builder → Kafka**, play *acks=1 lost an order*, then *Too strict to write*.

code: foreach (var b in isr) hw = Math.Min(hw, leo[b]);
foreach (var b in isr) hw = Math.Min(hw, leo[b]);

steps.prompt: A topic has **replication factor 3** and **`min.insync.replicas=3`**. Producers use `acks=all`. One broker is restarted for patching. What happens?
options: Writes to every partition that has a replica on that broker fail with `NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS` until it is back in the ISR
Nothing: two replicas are still alive
Kafka elects an out-of-sync replica so that writes continue
explain: `min.insync.replicas` equal to the replication factor means **no** broker may be down, so every rolling restart
becomes an outage for producers. Use `min.insync.replicas = RF - 1` (2 for RF 3): one broker of slack, and still two

steps.prompt: The payments service logs `ProduceException: Broker: Not enough in-sync replicas` for every message. You run the command below. What is going on?
code: Topic: payments  PartitionCount: 3  ReplicationFactor: 3  Configs: min.insync.replicas=2
Topic: payments  Partition: 0  Leader: 1  Replicas: 1,2,3  Isr: 1
Topic: payments  Partition: 1  Leader: 1  Replicas: 2,3,1  Isr: 1
Topic: payments  Partition: 2  Leader: 1  Replicas: 3,1,2  Isr: 1
options: Brokers 2 and 3 are down or not keeping up, so the ISR is only broker 1; with `min.insync.replicas=2` the leader rejects `acks=all` writes. Fix brokers 2 and 3, do not lower the setting
The topic has too few partitions; add partitions with `--alter`
The producer must switch to `acks=1` to fix the error permanently
The consumer group is lagging, which blocks producers
explain: `Isr: 1` while `Replicas: 1,2,3` means two followers fell out of sync (dead broker, full disk, network, overload).
The error is Kafka **protecting** you: with one copy, an acknowledged payment could be lost. Next steps:
broker logs and disk on brokers 2 and 3. Switching to `acks=1` or `min.insync.replicas=1` "fixes" it by accepting

items: `acks=1`, RF 3, the leader crashes right after answering
`acks=all`, `min.insync.replicas=1`, the ISR has shrunk to the leader, then its disk dies
`unclean.leader.election.enable=true` and an out-of-sync replica becomes leader
explain: Durability needs all three: `acks=all` (wait for the ISR), `min.insync.replicas >= 2` (the ISR may not shrink to
one copy) and clean leader election (never elect a replica that lacks committed records).

steps.prompt: Create a durable topic and a producer that uses it safely.
explain: RF 3 with `min.insync.replicas=2` tolerates one broker down. `Acks.All` waits for the ISR, and
`EnableIdempotence = true` must be set explicitly in Confluent.Kafka (librdkafka defaults it to false; the Java client
defaults it to true since 3.0). Idempotence requires `acks=all`.

steps.title: High watermark and ISR shrink
prompt: Write two methods the leader uses.
- `long HighWatermark(Dictionary<int, long> logEndOffsets, List<int> isr)`: the smallest log-end offset among the
brokers in the ISR (brokers outside the ISR do not count).
- `List<int> ShrinkIsr(List<int> isr, int leader, Dictionary<int, long> lastCaughtUpMs, long nowMs, long maxLagMs)`:
returns the ISR after the leader's check, in the same order. A follower stays when
`nowMs - lastCaughtUpMs[follower] <= maxLagMs`. The leader always stays (it may be missing from `lastCaughtUpMs`).
starter: long HighWatermark(Dictionary<int, long> logEndOffsets, List<int> isr)
List<int> ShrinkIsr(List<int> isr, int leader, Dictionary<int, long> lastCaughtUpMs, long nowMs, long maxLagMs)
solution: long HighWatermark(Dictionary<int, long> logEndOffsets, List<int> isr)
List<int> ShrinkIsr(List<int> isr, int leader, Dictionary<int, long> lastCaughtUpMs, long nowMs, long maxLagMs)
return isr.Where(b => b == leader || nowMs - lastCaughtUpMs[b] <= maxLagMs).ToList();
hints: `isr.Where(b => b == leader || nowMs - lastCaughtUpMs[b] <= maxLagMs)`: the `b == leader` test comes first so the dictionary is never read for the leader.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoLeo = new Dictionary<int, long> { [1] = 8, [2] = 8, [3] = 5 };
Dojo.Eq("HW is the slowest ISR member", 5L, HighWatermark(dojoLeo, new List<int> { 1, 2, 3 }));
Dojo.Eq("a replica outside the ISR does not hold the HW back", 8L, HighWatermark(dojoLeo, new List<int> { 1, 2 }));
var dojoSeen = new Dictionary<int, long> { [2] = 95000, [3] = 60000 };
Dojo.Eq("a follower 40 s behind leaves the ISR", new List<int> { 1, 2 }, ShrinkIsr(new List<int> { 1, 2, 3 }, 1, dojoSeen, 100000, 30000));
Dojo.Eq("exactly at the limit stays", new List<int> { 1, 3 }, ShrinkIsr(new List<int> { 1, 3 }, 1, dojoSeen, 90000, 30000));
Dojo.Eq("the leader always stays", new List<int> { 2 }, ShrinkIsr(new List<int> { 2, 3 }, 2, new Dictionary<int, long> { [3] = 0 }, 100000, 30000));

steps.title: Durability simulation: acks, ISR and leader failover
prompt: Simulate one partition and prove which writes survive a crash.
Write a class `ReplicatedPartition`:
- `ReplicatedPartition(int replicationFactor, int minInsync)`: brokers are numbered `1..replicationFactor`, all alive
and in the ISR; broker 1 leads.
- `int Leader` (get): the leader, or `-1` when the partition is offline.
- `List<int> Isr` (get): the ISR in ascending order.
- `string Produce(string value, string acks)` with `acks` `"0"`, `"1"` or `"all"`:
- offline → `"LEADER_NOT_AVAILABLE"`;
- `acks == "all"` and the ISR has fewer than `minInsync` brokers → `"NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS"` (nothing written);
- otherwise the leader appends. With `acks == "all"` every other ISR member copies the leader's whole log before the
answer. Return `"sent"` for `"0"`, otherwise `"ok offset {offset}"`.
- `void Replicate()`: every ISR follower copies the leader's whole log (a fetch round).
- `long HighWatermark`: the smallest log length in the ISR (0 when offline).
- `void Crash(int broker)`: the broker dies and leaves the ISR at once (a simplification of
`replica.lag.time.max.ms`). If it was the leader, the **lowest-numbered** remaining ISR member becomes leader
(clean election), or `-1` if the ISR is empty; every remaining ISR follower then truncates its log to the new
leader's length.
- `List<string> Committed()`: the leader's records below the high watermark (what consumers can read).
starter: public string Produce(string value, string acks) => "";
solution: public int Leader { get; private set; } = 1;
public string Produce(string value, string acks)
hints: Keep a `Dictionary<int, List<string>>` of logs, one per broker.
With `acks == "all"`, call `Replicate()` after the leader appends: every other ISR member copies the leader's log.
On a leader crash: `Leader = Isr.Count > 0 ? Isr.Min() : -1`, then cut longer follower logs to the new leader's length.
template: var dojoP = new ReplicatedPartition(3, 2);
Dojo.Eq("broker 1 leads", 1, dojoP.Leader);
Dojo.Eq("acks=1 is answered by the leader alone", "ok offset 0", dojoP.Produce("order-1", "1"));
Dojo.Eq("followers have not fetched yet: HW 0", 0L, dojoP.HighWatermark);
dojoP.Crash(1);
Dojo.Eq("broker 2 takes over", 2, dojoP.Leader);
Dojo.Eq("the ISR shrinks", new List<int> { 2, 3 }, dojoP.Isr);
Dojo.Eq("the acknowledged order-1 is gone (acks=1 lost an order)", new List<string>(), dojoP.Committed());
Dojo.Eq("acks=all waits for the ISR", "ok offset 0", dojoP.Produce("order-2", "all"));
Dojo.Eq("acks=all data is committed at once", new List<string> { "order-2" }, dojoP.Committed());
dojoP.Crash(2);
Dojo.Eq("broker 3 takes over", 3, dojoP.Leader);
Dojo.Eq("acks=all data survives the leader crash", new List<string> { "order-2" }, dojoP.Committed());
Dojo.Eq("one replica left: acks=all is refused", "NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS", dojoP.Produce("order-3", "all"));
Dojo.Eq("min.insync.replicas does not apply to acks=1", "ok offset 1", dojoP.Produce("order-4", "1"));
dojoP.Crash(3);
Dojo.Eq("no ISR left: offline", -1, dojoP.Leader);
Dojo.Eq("offline partition", "LEADER_NOT_AVAILABLE", dojoP.Produce("order-5", "all"));
Dojo.Eq("nothing is readable while offline", new List<string>(), dojoP.Committed());
var dojoQ = new ReplicatedPartition(3, 2);
Dojo.Eq("acks=0 gets no answer", "sent", dojoQ.Produce("x", "0"));
Dojo.Eq("not committed before a fetch round", 0L, dojoQ.HighWatermark);
dojoQ.Replicate();
Dojo.Eq("a fetch round moves the HW", 1L, dojoQ.HighWatermark);
dojoQ.Crash(3);
Dojo.Eq("a follower crash does not change the leader", 1, dojoQ.Leader);
Dojo.Eq("two left: acks=all still works", "ok offset 1", dojoQ.Produce("y", "all"));
